# RC-001 QLD8 second-order fermion-EOM map for the Higgs-source Laplacians

**Date:** 2026-11-10  
**Scope:** reduce the endpoint Laplacians generated by the exact source-square IBP identity using the leading renormalizable fermion EOMs. This exposes the resulting Higgs-derivative and gauge-field-strength four-fermion structures. It does not eliminate the mixed derivative term, perform the complete Fierz/IBP basis reduction, or calculate loop counterterms.

## 1. Covariant Dirac-square identity and sign

Use
\[
D_\mu=\partial_\mu+i\mathcal A_\mu,\qquad
[D_\mu,D_\nu]=i\mathscr F_{\mu\nu},\qquad
\sigma^{\mu\nu}=\frac{i}{2}[\gamma^\mu,\gamma^\nu],
\]
with \(g_{\mu\nu}=(+---)\). Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
\slashed D^2
&=D^2+\frac14[\gamma^\mu,\gamma^\nu][D_\mu,D_\nu]\\
&=D^2+\frac12\sigma^{\mu\nu}\mathscr F_{\mu\nu},
\end{aligned}
\]
so
\[
\boxed{D^2\psi=\slashed D^2\psi-\frac12\sigma^{\mu\nu}\mathscr F_{\mu\nu}\psi.}
\]
The sign follows from the stated \(D_\mu=\partial_\mu+i\mathcal A_\mu\) convention. For barred fields use the conjugate left-acting covariant derivative and the conjugate representation curvature; do not copy the unbarred matrix ordering without conjugation.

## 2. Curvatures of the renormalizable source fields

All quarks and the electron fields are neutral under the model's \(U(1)_X\). Their curvatures are
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathscr F_Q^{\mu\nu}
&=g_sG^{A\mu\nu}T^A
+g_2W^{I\mu\nu}\frac{\tau^I}{2}
+g'\frac16B^{\mu\nu},\\
\mathscr F_u^{\mu\nu}
&=g_sG^{A\mu\nu}T^A
+g'\frac23B^{\mu\nu},\\
\mathscr F_d^{\mu\nu}
&=g_sG^{A\mu\nu}T^A
-g'\frac13B^{\mu\nu},\\
\mathscr F_{L_e}^{\mu\nu}
&=g_2W^{I\mu\nu}\frac{\tau^I}{2}
-g'\frac12B^{\mu\nu},\\
\mathscr F_{e_R}^{\mu\nu}
&=-g'B^{\mu\nu}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The weak generators act only on doublets and the color generators only on quarks. There is no \(g_XF_X^{\mu\nu}\) term in these five curvatures. The dimension-five \(\mu,\tau\) source is outside this strict \(M_E^{-4}\) reduction.

## 3. Second-order EOMs from the leading first-order EOMs

The leading renormalizable EOMs are
\[
\begin{aligned}
i\slashed D Q_L&=Y_u\widetilde H\,u_R+Y_dH\,d_R,\\
i\slashed D u_R&=Y_u^\dagger\widetilde H^\dagger Q_L,\\
i\slashed D d_R&=Y_d^\dagger H^\dagger Q_L,\\
i\slashed D L_e&=y_eH e_R,\\
i\slashed D e_R&=y_e^*H^\dagger L_e.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \(i\slashed D\psi=\mathcal Y_\psi\) implies \(\slashed D\psi=-i\mathcal Y_\psi\), applying \(-i\slashed D\) to the right-hand side and using the Dirac-square identity gives
\[
\boxed{\begin{aligned}
D^2Q_L={}&-i\gamma^\mu\big[
(D_\mu\widetilde H)Y_u u_R
+\widetilde H Y_uD_\mu u_R\\
&\qquad\qquad
+(D_\mu H)Y_d d_R
+H Y_dD_\mu d_R\big]
-\frac12\sigma^{\mu\nu}\mathscr F_{Q,\mu\nu}Q_L,\\[1mm]
D^2u_R={}&-i\gamma^\mu\big[
(D_\mu\widetilde H^\dagger)Y_u^\dagger Q_L
+\widetilde H^\dagger Y_u^\dagger D_\mu Q_L\big]
-\frac12\sigma^{\mu\nu}\mathscr F_{u,\mu\nu}u_R,\\[1mm]
D^2d_R={}&-i\gamma^\mu\big[
(D_\mu H^\dagger)Y_d^\dagger Q_L
+H^\dagger Y_d^\dagger D_\mu Q_L\big]
-\frac12\sigma^{\mu\nu}\mathscr F_{d,\mu\nu}d_R,\\[1mm]
D^2L_e={}&-iy_e\gamma^\mu\big[
(D_\mu H)e_R+H D_\mu e_R\big]
-\frac12\sigma^{\mu\nu}\mathscr F_{L_e,\mu\nu}L_e,\\[1mm]
D^2e_R={}&-iy_e^*\gamma^\mu\big[
(D_\mu H^\dagger)L_e+H^\dagger D_\mu L_e\big]
-\frac12\sigma^{\mu\nu}\mathscr F_{e_R,\mu\nu}e_R.
\end{aligned}}
\]
The flavor matrices are constant in spacetime. The derivatives on \(H,\widetilde H\) and on partner fermions are retained.

## 4. Substitution into the source Laplacians

For \(J=\bar fY\chi\),
\[
D^2J=(D^2\bar f)Y\chi
+2(D_\mu\bar f)Y D^\mu\chi
+\bar fY D^2\chi.
\]
The two endpoint terms are reduced with the conjugate/unbarred second-order EOMs in §3. They generate:
- four-fermion operators with one Higgs field and one covariant Higgs derivative, from the \(\gamma^\mu D_\mu H\) terms;
- four-fermion operators with one gauge-field strength, from \(\sigma^{\mu\nu}\mathscr F_{\mu\nu}\);
- terms with derivatives on the partner fermions, which must be kept until a separate IBP/EOM basis reduction.

The middle term
\[
2(D_\mu\bar f)Y D^\mu\chi
\]
is not removed by the first-order Dirac EOM: it contains free-index derivatives, not their gamma traces. It remains an independent derivative class until an explicit IBP/Fierz reduction is completed.

### 4.1 Evanescent-basis enlargement after second-order EOM substitution

The four minimal differences \(E_{RL}^{(0)},E_{LR}^{(0)},E_{RR}^{(0)},E_{LL}^{(0)}\) defined for the original scalar-times-scalar source pairs are **not** a closed evanescent set after applying the second-order EOM. The \(\gamma^\mu D_\mu H\) terms generate scalar/vector spinor products, and the curvature terms generate scalar/tensor products with explicit \(F_{\mu\nu}\). Each new Dirac tensor product must be Fierz-reduced in the same NDR convention and supplied with its own \(D\)-dimensional Fierz-difference evanescent definition. If one-loop renormalization generates longer antisymmetrized gamma strings, those must also be included.

Accordingly, the present note fixes the Dirac-square identity and exposes the operator classes, but does not claim a closed d-dimensional counterterm basis for the EOM-reduced operators. The UV and EFT sides must use the same enlarged evanescent set before finite matching.

Combining §2 with the source-pair Fierz map is mandatory. For example, the curvature terms contain both color and electroweak field strengths for the quark channels; the lepton channel contains only hypercharge and weak field strengths. No \(U(1)_X\) curvature occurs in the retained renormalizable source sector.

## 5. Consequence for the source-square operator and PR #69

The covariant IBP identity
\[
(D_\mu J_A^\dagger)(D^\mu J_B)\doteq-J_A^\dagger D^2J_B
\]
therefore reorganizes, but does not eliminate, the dimension-eight source-square term. The second-order EOM trades endpoint Laplacians for Higgs-derivative and field-strength four-fermion operators; the mixed derivative term remains.

These are four-fermion/current-sector operators. This tree-level EOM rearrangement does not generate a direct local \(hh\), \(hs\), or \(ss\) two-point coefficient. Any indirect contribution through loops or EFT soft insertions requires its own same-order matching and counterterm analysis; it is not inferred to vanish here.

## 6. Validation boundary

The companion exact-arithmetic audit checks the Dirac-square curvature coefficient/sign using explicit four-dimensional gamma matrices, the hypercharge of each renormalizable Higgs source, and the absence of \(U(1)_X\) charge for all retained source fermions. It does not numerically evaluate Wilson coefficients or claim the full one-loop evanescent counterterm basis.


## 7. Fierz closure for the EOM-generated Dirac structures

The scalar–vector and scalar–tensor products generated by the second-order EOM are now treated explicitly in [RC-001-QLD-EOM-generated-chiral-Fierz-identities.md](RC-001-QLD-EOM-generated-chiral-Fierz-identities.md). This adds exact four-dimensional Fierz projections for all \(P_{R,L}\otimes\gamma^\mu P_{R,L}\) combinations, both opposite-chirality \(P_R\otimes\sigma^{\mu\nu}P_L\) and \(P_L\otimes\sigma^{\mu\nu}P_R\) combinations, and the two same-chirality scalar–tensor channels in a three-component chiral tensor basis.

The exact SymPy audit checks 34 matrix identities (8704/8704 components) and six chiral tensor self-duality relations. The associated d-dimensional Fierz-difference operators are defined by subtracting the four-dimensional **operator-level** projection, including the Grassmann minus sign and preserving derivative/field-strength labels.

This closes the displayed four-dimensional spinor projections, not the one-loop evanescent mixing matrix. Longer gamma strings generated by UV poles remain to be added if they occur.
